name: octane_combustion_400pct_air
title: Combustion of octane with 400 % theoretical air
summary: Octane burned with 400 % theoretical air in steady flow: adiabatic flame temperature from the first law on the combustion reaction (formation enthalpies), fuel-air ratio and stoichiometric dosage; excess-air effect on the flame temperature.

authors: TBD (ULiège, course Thermodynamique appliquée MECA0002 repetition team)

verification.summary: Compared with the solution stored in the original EES file: the 3 flagged variables are unit-annotation artifacts and the maximum relative deviation is 2.2e-4 on `TAF` (688.56 vs 688.71 °C).
verification.reference: EES stored solution of the source file (compare_solution.py --ees-units)
verification.notes: 35 common variables, 3 differ (rtol=0.001) - all 3 are unit-annotation artifacts, hand-checked (h_H2O_*_bis stored without units in kJ/kg: 8.7e-5; TAF_K stored in K but converted by the tool: 1.5e-4). Max over all common variables 2.2e-4 on TAF (CoolProp's ideal-gas enthalpy rise vs EES; the absolute species enthalpies h_CO2_*, h_H2O_* agree with the stored values within 1.4e-4). Stale EES records x, y, mm ignored. Comparison made with the solution of the earlier runnable variant (MM_f = 114.23), which the native file reproduces to 8.8e-6 (molarmass(C8H18) = 114.229 in CoolSolve; TAF identical; CoolSolve 0.3.0@4798e2b).
